severities.label: Important
severities.description: Serious bug or weakness without immediate exploitation

releases.title: Mac notifications next to the iPhone app, and FFmpeg 8.1.3
releases.summary: On a Mac that also has Khandaq for iPhone installed, macOS refused the Mac app's message notifications, because both apps carried the same identifier. The Mac app now has its own. The Windows, Mac and Linux apps carry FFmpeg 8.1.3, the newest release of the 8.1 line.

changes.title: New-message notifications show on a Mac that also has Khandaq for iPhone
changes.description: Macs with Apple silicon can install the iPhone app, and it shares the identifier org.khandaq.messenger with the Mac app. On such a Mac, macOS took the Mac app for the iPhone app and refused its notifications without a word. The Mac app is now org.khandaq.desktop. Your profiles, settings and history stay where they are, but macOS meets the app as a new one once: it asks again before showing notifications, before the first call uses the microphone or the camera, and before you share your screen. If you let the app open your profile without asking for its password, macOS also asks once whether Khandaq may use the password it keeps in the keychain: enter your Mac password and choose Always Allow. If Khandaq for iPhone is in your Applications folder, it holds the name Khandaq there, so keep the Mac app in another folder, for example the Applications folder in your home folder, and do not let Finder replace one with the other.

changes.title: FFmpeg 8.1.3 in the Windows, Mac and Linux apps
changes.description: The three desktop apps read voice messages, the camera and video calls with FFmpeg 8.1.3, the newest release of the 8.1 line, built as before with only the parts the app uses. NVD lists 16 advisories against 8.1.3, down from 35 against 8.1.1. The MP4 reader still skips the kinds of boxes with known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678).

releases.title: Voice messages play in the Windows app
releases.summary: The Windows app plays voice messages from the phones in the chat, as the Mac and Linux apps do, instead of opening them in the system's player. It now carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 built for it, like the Mac and Linux apps, in place of FFmpeg 4.4.8.

changes.title: Voice messages from the phones play in the Windows app
The Windows app carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 built for it, like the Mac and Linux apps

releases.title: Files from contacts wait for you to accept them
releases.summary: A new installation no longer saves the files a contact sends you by itself: each one waits in the chat until you accept it. The Linux app reads voice messages with an FFmpeg built for it, which skips the parts of MP4 files with known bugs, instead of Ubuntu's FFmpeg 6.1.1.

changes.title: Files from a contact wait for Accept on a new installation
changes.description: Until now a new installation saved every file a contact sent you into the downloads folder by itself, before you had looked at it. Now it starts with Settings > Network > Download attachments set to Never: each file waits in the chat until you press Accept. Always and Small files are still there to choose, and an installation that already has a choice keeps it. A folder you set for a contact still takes their files, and files sent in a group are saved as before.

changes.title: Voice messages on Linux are read with a hardened FFmpeg
changes.description: The Linux app used Ubuntu's FFmpeg 6.1.1 with every format Ubuntu builds in, and Ubuntu has not yet fixed CVE-2026-107678 in it: a crafted MP4 file can make FFmpeg exhaust its stack, and a voice message is an MP4 file the app reads when you press play. The Linux app now carries FFmpeg 8.1.1 with only the parts it uses for the camera, voice messages and video calls, with no network access and no filters. As in the Mac app, its MP4 reader skips the kinds of boxes that have known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678). The libraries that came only with Ubuntu's FFmpeg are gone too, so the portable archive shrinks from 123 MB to about 50 MB.

releases.title: The Mac app is built for macOS 11 and later again
releases.summary: Khandaq v0.2.47 for Mac asked for macOS 11 but did not open on macOS 11 to 15: its libraries had been built for macOS 26. This release builds them for macOS 11 and checks every file in the app before packing it. The Windows and Linux builds get the call checks written in August, which had never reached them, and pictures you receive are read with a fixed libexif on Windows and Mac.

changes.title: The Mac app is built for macOS 11 and later
changes.description: v0.2.47 took its libraries from a package manager that builds them for the newest macOS, so on macOS 11 to 15 the app did not open. Every library in the app now targets macOS 11, and the build refuses to pack the app if any file in it needs a newer macOS or loads a library from outside the app. It has been run on macOS 26; on macOS 11 to 15 it is checked file by file, not yet by running it. Profiles and message history from v0.2.47 open as before. The app is still for Macs with Apple Silicon and is still not notarized.

changes.title: Calls on Windows and Linux get the packet checks
changes.description: In August the app got checks on the packets that carry a call: a packet whose header claims more data than it holds is dropped before anything is copied, and so is an audio packet too short to carry any sound. Without them, a contact in a call could send packets that make the app write past the end of a buffer. The Windows and Linux builds compiled an unchanged copy of the network library and never got these checks. They are built from the patched copy now, like the Mac app.

changes.title: Received pictures are read with libexif 0.6.26
changes.description: To show a received photo the right way up, the app reads the camera information inside it with libexif. Up to 0.6.25, libexif could be made to crash, or to leak memory contents, by a picture carrying crafted Fuji or Olympus maker notes (CVE-2026-40386). 0.6.26 fixes that and two related bugs (CVE-2026-32775, CVE-2026-40385).

changes.title: Less of FFmpeg and a newer PCRE2 in the Mac app
changes.description: The Mac app used to carry all of FFmpeg. It now carries only the parts it uses for the camera, voice messages and video calls, with no network access and no filters. Its MP4 reader no longer reads three kinds of boxes a voice message never contains, which have known bugs and no fixed FFmpeg 8.1 release yet (CVE-2026-52297, CVE-2026-96611, CVE-2026-107678). PCRE2 moves to 10.49.

releases.title: The new look on the computer, with requests that wait for your answer
releases.summary: Khandaq for Windows, macOS and Linux gets the look the phones got in v0.2.46: one list with the people online now first, and a conversation that says before you send whether a message goes now or waits in transit. Rebuilding every screen turned up older problems as well, fixed here: the computer accepted every contact request by itself and threw its message away, turning off Keep history lost messages still waiting to be sent, and a profile with a few hundred contacts took half a minute to open. Replies, edits and reactions from phones now show on the computer, which does not send them yet.

changes.title: One list, with the people online now first
changes.description: Chats, contacts and groups are one list instead of tabs: people online now first, then everyone else, and your notes for yourself last. The line under your name says how this computer is connected: directly, through a relay, or not at all. An ID pasted into the search line opens New contact. The interface is set in IBM Plex Sans, in a light and a dark theme that follows the system unless you choose one, in place of the ten old colour schemes.

changes.title: Contact requests wait for your answer
changes.description: The computer used to accept every contact request by itself, without asking, and threw away the message that came with it. A request now waits as a card at the top of the list until you answer, with the person's message, the start of their key, Accept and Decline, and it is still there after a restart. Decline sends nothing and can be undone for 5 seconds. A group invitation comes as the same kind of card, with Join.

changes.title: A message to someone offline waits in transit and goes once
changes.description: A message for someone who is offline waits in a tray above the field and leaves on its own when they are back; before you send, the line under the field says which will happen. Waiting messages are kept in your profile, through this update too, even with Keep history turned off, which used to lose them when you quit. A message is no longer sent again and again when its receipt goes missing, or twice after a reconnect.

changes.title: The contact card shows how you are connected
changes.description: Clicking the name at the top of a conversation unfolds the person's card: whether you reach each other directly or through a relay, when they were online over the last day, Mute, key verification, their key with a QR code, the files you exchanged, and Block and Remove behind one question. These marks stay on this computer; requests from a blocked key are dropped, and Settings can unblock it. Remove now also deletes the conversation from this computer, as on the phones.

changes.title: Moving a profile in no longer replaces one with the same name
changes.description: Importing a profile copied the file under its own name and, after one question, replaced a profile with that name, leaving that profile's settings and history next to the new file; nothing showed whose profile it was, and it did not open afterwards. Move a profile from another device now reads the file first, asks for its password if it has one, shows the name and the ID, adds the profile under a name of its own and opens it.

changes.title: A profile with hundreds of contacts opens in seconds
changes.description: Opening a profile sorted the contact list again for every contact it loaded. In a test with 311 contacts and about 10,000 messages, the window now appears after about 3 seconds instead of 30, and Khandaq uses about 55 MB less memory.

changes.title: Logging out no longer ends in a crash
changes.description: After Log out, closing the sign-in window made Khandaq crash as it quit. It now quits normally. Log out also says what it means before it happens, and from then on every start opens sign-in until you log in again, even with a saved password.

changes.title: Sign-in says why a profile did not open
changes.description: Any failure at sign-in showed the same Wrong password box. Sign-in now tells apart a wrong password, a damaged profile file, a file it may not read, a profile already open in Khandaq on this computer and a proxy that did not work, and says under the field what to do. Forgot the password? says it cannot be recovered and what happens to the old file. A new profile takes three pages: a name, a password or none with what each means, and your ID.

changes.title: Files, voice messages and calls are part of the conversation
changes.description: A file is an entry in the conversation with its state in words and its size in KB or MB, and a picture shows inside the conversation. A voice message from a phone shows its length, with Listen. A call runs in a bar at the top of the conversation and leaves an entry such as Call, 0:09, Missed call or No answer. Calling someone offline says the call will not get through and offers to wait and call; groups say they have no calls.

changes.title: Groups say who gets a message now
changes.description: A group's header counts members and who is online now, and a strip under it shows who gets a message right away. An observer sees Read only in place of the message field. The group card names roles in words, and the founder and moderators change roles and remove members after one question. New group is one panel with a name and a choice between By invitation only and open; before, every new group was open and called New group.

changes.title: Replies, edits and reactions from phones show on the computer
changes.description: A reply from a phone shows with the message it answers. In groups, edits, deletions and reactions from phones show too; in one-to-one chats they show for files, not yet for text. The computer does not send replies, edits or reactions yet: a quote from the computer reaches phones as plain text. A message in a form this version cannot show says so instead of showing its code.

changes.title: News from other chats comes inside the window
changes.description: While Khandaq is in front, a message from another chat, a contact request or a group invitation slides in as a band under the top bar, and a click opens it; before, the system showed a notification even with the window open. A request no longer shows the sender's whole 64-character key as its title. Errors and questions appear over the Khandaq window and name what failed, instead of boxes in the middle of the screen.

changes.title: Settings in plain sections
changes.description: Settings are sections with each value at the right of its row: the theme as System, Light or Dark, notifications, privacy with blocked keys, profile transfer, network and About. Download attachments now works: Always, Small files up to a size you set, or Never; the old Accept files automatically box did nothing. Restoring defaults resets only the network settings; before, it deleted the profile's settings file with the names and notes you gave contacts. The update check box that did nothing is gone.

changes.title: The connection, in words
changes.description: Clicking the line under your name opens Network in Settings: how this computer is connected and what that means for messages, whether it has internet, and how many relays and contacts it reaches directly, with no IP addresses. While it looks for the network it offers Connect again and asks every 15 seconds, instead of about every second. The log for support starts with the state of the network, also without addresses.

changes.title: Every screen works from the keyboard
changes.description: Tab goes through every screen in reading order and back to the start, and the control in focus always shows a ring; a panel open over the list or the conversation keeps Tab to itself until it closes. Screen readers get a name for every icon button, chat, request card and message. Every screen was checked at 1440 by 900, 1920 by 1080 and the smallest window, in both themes, and text that was cut off now wraps. With Reduce motion on, nothing slides.

changes.title: Russian, Arabic and Chinese throughout
changes.description: Every new string is in English, Russian, Arabic and Chinese, and the older ones in these languages were cleaned up: plural forms, labels left untranslated, and words the app no longer uses, such as friend, or account for the profile. Arabic runs right to left, and Russian or English text inside it keeps its own direction. German, French and the other older translations do not have the new strings yet, so the new screens show English in them.

changes.title: Your ID as a QR code in You
changes.description: Your photo, name and status are edited in place in You, beside a QR code of your ID with Copy ID, Copy QR code and Save QR code. New profiles start without a status, and the joke status that older versions set by themselves is cleared once; a status you wrote stays.

changes.title: Smaller fixes found while rebuilding the screens
changes.description: Text between triple backticks now shows as code. A mention by a name written in Cyrillic or Arabic now highlights. Sizes count 1,000 bytes to the KB, as on the phones. The language menu names each language in its own words, and a request from a tox: link offers the greeting of New contact instead of the old joke text.

releases.title: A new look built around one question: will your message get through
releases.summary: Khandaq on iPhone and Android has a new look. The main screen puts the people who are online now first, a message to someone who is offline waits in transit and leaves on its own once they are back, and the line under the message field says which will happen before you send. Rebuilding every screen turned up older problems as well, fixed here: on iPhone a voice message could go on recording after you let go of the button, and on Android a profile file that could not be read made the app start under a new ID. The desktop app gets the same look in its own release.

changes.title: One list, with the people online now first
changes.description: Chats, contacts and requests are one list instead of tabs. People who are online now come first, then everyone else, and your notes for yourself stay last. Requests, messages in transit and Favorites each have a filter over the list. The line under your name says how your phone is connected: directly, through a relay, or not at all. The interface is set in IBM Plex Sans, in a light and a dark theme that follows the system unless you choose one.

changes.title: A message to someone offline waits in transit and goes on its own
changes.description: Before you send, the line under the message field says whether the message goes right away or waits because the person is offline. A waiting message stays on your phone in a tray above the field and leaves on its own when they come online; the tray says how many are waiting. A message the network refused is marked Not sent, with Retry.

changes.title: The contact card shows how you are connected
changes.description: Tapping a name in a conversation opens its card: whether your devices reach each other directly or through a relay right now, when the person was online over the last day as seen from this device, their key for verification, the files you exchanged, Mute, and Block and Remove behind a confirmation. Mute and Block stay on this device.

changes.title: A voice message records only while you hold the button
changes.description: The first time you held the microphone button, iPhone asked for access to the microphone. The answer came after your finger had left the button, and the recording started anyway and went on with nothing on screen until the next hold. A recording now starts only while the button is still held, and with access denied a hold says why and offers Settings.

changes.title: Sharing into Khandaq works on iPhone
changes.description: Choosing Khandaq in another app's share sheet never got past Preparing share: the extension had no storage shared with the app to leave things in. It now passes on a link, text, photo or file, and Khandaq asks which chat it goes to, in the order of Forward. A long text goes in parts that each fit a message. iOS does not let a share extension open its app, so it says to open Khandaq.

changes.title: An unreadable profile file no longer starts the app under a new ID
changes.description: When the profile file could not be read, a saved session still opened by itself and the network started without your profile, under a new ID with no contacts. The app now checks the profile files before it opens them, stops on sign-in with No access to the profile file and a code for support, and writes nothing to the disk.

changes.title: Forgot the password removes everything it should
changes.description: Forgot the password left the stored files and the network save behind, so the next profile stopped on Wrong credentials. It now removes them, sign-in explains what happened, and Delete and create new starts a clean profile with a new ID. A phone that is stuck after the old flow gets out the same way.

changes.title: A profile without a password is sealed with a key from a secure source
changes.description: Khandaq on Android seals a profile created without a password with a random key that the Android Keystore protects. That key came from a general-purpose random generator; it now comes from SecureRandom. Profiles created earlier keep the key they have; setting a password in Settings seals such a profile again with your password.

changes.title: Group headers show who is online as it changes
changes.description: On iPhone the network engine reported changes in a group, such as members joining or coming online, where no screen was listening. A group opened on a real profile kept the members and presence it found on opening, so right after joining it said 1 member. The header, the member list and the chat list now follow those changes.

changes.title: Screens adapt to the largest text sizes
changes.description: Every screen was checked at the largest accessibility text sizes and in Arabic and Chinese. Text wraps at its words instead of being cut or broken inside a word. On iPhone the time moves above the message and secondary lines fold away so the conversation keeps room, and holding a button or a cut name shows it large, as the system bars do.

changes.title: No network shows within seconds
changes.description: On Android the line under your name said No network only once the network engine gave up, about 25 seconds after the phone lost its connection. It now follows the phone's own network and says so in about 2.5 seconds.

changes.title: Leaving a member's screen keeps your draft
changes.description: Leaving the screen of a group member sent whatever was typed in the private message field, even half a sentence, and cleared it even when sending failed. Leaving now keeps the draft; only Send sends.

changes.title: Replies from iPhone read as replies
changes.description: A reply whose header arrived without its closing marker showed on Android as plain text with the header in it. It is now read as a reply, as iPhone reads it.

changes.title: Permission requests name every use, in your language
changes.description: The microphone request on iPhone named only calls; it now names voice messages and videos too. In Arabic and Chinese the camera, microphone, photos, Face ID and location requests were in English and are now translated.

changes.title: Smaller fixes found while rebuilding the screens
changes.description: In Arabic the back arrows on iPhone point the right way and About names Khandaq. On Android a group joined from an invitation shows its name before it connects instead of a code, a mention stays visible in the dark theme, and a link in an older group chat asks in your language before it opens.

changes.title: khandaq.org has the new look
changes.description: The site shares the apps' colours and type, works without JavaScript, follows the system theme, and shows screens of the new app in English and Russian.

releases.title: Six problems testers ran into in everyday chats
releases.summary: Testers sent us six reports in one afternoon: a video that vanished once it was sent, a message that showed up twice, an Enter key that sent half-written text, a share sheet without Favorites, an English screen in the middle of a call, and an Edit action some people never saw. Each one was reproduced on a real phone before it was fixed, and checking the fixes turned up two more: a photo shared to a contact could quietly land in Favorites instead, and a caption written for a group photo never appeared in the sender's own chat.

changes.title: A video you send no longer disappears once it has gone out
changes.description: While a video was uploading it showed a progress bubble; the moment the upload finished, that bubble was replaced by one with no width at all, so only the time and the ticks were left. The other person received the video normally. The finished video now always gets a proper preview, and a video whose first frame cannot be decoded on the phone shows a dark tile with a play button instead of nothing.

changes.title: Text sent after a photo no longer appears twice
changes.description: Khandaq shows a text sent right after a photo as that photo's caption. It decided this partly by when each message was received, and for your own messages that time is empty until the other side confirms delivery, so any text sent after a photo — even minutes later — counted as its caption. When the confirmation arrived the text became a separate message again, but the photo kept showing it too, until the chat was reopened. Your own captions are now matched only by when they were sent, and the photo and the text below it are always redrawn together, including when one of them is edited or deleted.

changes.title: A photo shared to a contact could be saved to Favorites instead of being sent
changes.description: When a photo was shared from the gallery to a contact while Favorites was the chat last opened in Khandaq, the app looked at the open chat rather than at the contact you picked, saved the photo to Favorites and never sent it. The contact you pick now always gets the file.

changes.title: Your caption on a group photo now shows up for you too
changes.description: A caption typed under a photo or video sent to a group is sent once the file has gone out. When it went out straight away it reached everyone in the group but was never written down on the sender's own phone, so the sender never saw their own caption, not even after reopening the chat. It is now kept like any other message and shown inside the photo it belongs to.

changes.title: Enter starts a new line
changes.description: On Samsung Keyboard, and on any other keyboard that sends Enter as a key press, the Enter key sent the message, so a message could not be split into lines. Enter on the on-screen keyboard now starts a new line; the send button sends. A physical keyboard keeps Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a new line.

changes.title: Favorites in the share sheet
changes.description: Sharing from the gallery or another app listed only contacts and groups. Favorites is now first in that list: files are saved straight into it and shared text opens there ready to send. Backing out of the list now closes it instead of leaving an empty screen behind, and a share that arrives before Khandaq is unlocked opens the app instead of an empty list.

changes.title: Edit is always there for your own messages
changes.description: The Edit action was hidden whenever a particular message could not be edited — still waiting to be delivered, sent to an app without edit support, a long message sent in parts, a reply, or older than 48 hours — which looked as if editing did not exist on some phones. It is now a pencil in the selection bar for every message of yours, and when an edit is not possible it says why. Call entries in the chat are not messages and do not offer it. The selection bar shows just the number of selected messages instead of English text.

changes.title: The call waiting screen is translated
changes.description: Calling a contact who is offline showed "waiting for friend … to come online" in English whatever the app language. It now reads in Russian, Arabic and Chinese as well.

changes.title: Two more waits on the audio engine have a time limit
changes.description: The 0.2.44 freeze fix bounded the wait for the device's audio engine in the recording path. Two other places waited for the same signal with no limit at all; they now share the same deadline. Nothing changes when the audio engine starts normally.

releases.title: The app could stop responding, and nothing could bring it back
releases.summary: Google Play measures how often an app stops responding. For Khandaq that figure had risen well past the level Play considers acceptable, while the number of outright crashes stayed at zero — nothing was failing, something was getting stuck. It was one wait that had no way of ever finishing. The same release also removes two pieces of work the app was doing on the screen's own thread that it did not need to do at all.

changes.title: Leaving a group call can no longer freeze the app
changes.description: When a call starts, one part of the app waits for the device's audio engine to come up before it begins recording. That wait watched a single signal — and that signal is set by a different part of the app, only once the engine has actually started. On a device where the engine failed to start, it was never set, and the wait had no other way to end: asking it to stop set something the wait did not look at, and shutting the engine down set the very value it was waiting to leave. Closing the call screen then waited for that stuck part to finish before doing anything else, with no time limit, so the whole app stopped responding and stayed that way. The wait now stops when it is asked to and gives up after a few seconds, the audio system is released instead of being left unusable until the app is restarted, and every place where the screen waits for a background task to finish now has a time limit. Nothing else about calls changes.

changes.title: Sending a group message no longer goes through the whole member list first
changes.description: Every message sent to a group was checked for mentions by walking the group's entire membership before looking at the message at all — work that reads from the encrypted database and grows with the size of the group, done on the same thread that draws the screen, for messages that mention nobody. A mention has to start with an @ sign, so a message without one is now recognised as having no mentions without any of that work. Mentions themselves behave exactly as before.

changes.title: Setting up notifications no longer slows the rest of the app down
changes.description: The previous releases added a separate notification permission for each contact, registered in the background. Each registration waited for a reply from the notification server by re-reading the local database four times a second for up to thirty seconds, and one of these ran per contact at the same time. All of them share a single connection to that database with the screen itself, and requests are served strictly in the order they arrive, so the screen ended up queued behind them — which is what made the delays above long enough to be noticed. The reply is now passed directly to whatever is waiting for it, the database is consulted only occasionally as a fallback, and no more than two registrations run at once. Notifications are unaffected; a registration that does not get through is retried the next time that contact comes online, exactly as before.

releases.title: A filename could point somewhere it had no business pointing
releases.summary: Two of the fixes below share a shape: a check that existed, written down and working, applied to one code path and not to its neighbour. The filename rule was on every 1:1 transfer and missing from one kind of group transfer. The audio length check was in all three copies of the source and in none of the Android builds, because Android does not build from that source. Neither gap was visible by reading the fix; both are now held by tests that fail when a path stops being covered.

changes.title: A file sent to a group can no longer name a file somewhere else
changes.description: Whoever sends a file picks its name, and for one kind of group transfer that name was stored exactly as it arrived. The file itself was saved safely — but the stored name was later joined to a folder, and one of the places doing that reads the file and sends its contents to whoever asked for the group's history. A name pointing up and out of the group's folder therefore read an unrelated file and handed it over: attachments from other conversations, avatars, anything small enough to fit in one packet. The same name was also used as both source and destination when saving a file out of the app. Names are now cleaned before they are stored, the name shown in the chat is still the one the sender chose, and the three places that pass a file's contents onward refuse any path that leaves its own folder. Records already saved by older versions are covered by that refusal. The other two clients were never affected: they keep the display name and the path apart.

changes.title: Android calls now actually carry the audio length check
changes.description: An earlier release added a check that an audio packet is long enough before its first four bytes are read. It went into all three copies of the underlying library — and Android kept shipping without it, because the Android build does not use those copies: it fetches the library fresh from upstream and compiles that. Editing the source in this repository could not reach the file that ships. The check is now applied during the build itself, for every processor type, and the native library has been rebuilt so the shipped one carries it.

changes.title: A password with a quote in it no longer locks you out of your own database
changes.description: When changing the password that protects the local database, the new password was placed into a database command without escaping, while the command that opens the database escaped it. For a password containing a quote character the two disagreed: the database could be re-encrypted under a shortened form of the password, and the app would then try to open it with the full one and fail. Both commands now escape identically, and a check keeps them that way.

changes.title: Private groups no longer announce their identifier to every friend
changes.description: While reconnecting to a group, the app asks friends who are in it to invite it back. Since the previous release the receiving side refuses that request for private groups — knowing a private group's identifier is not the same as being a member. The sending side kept asking anyway, which handed that identifier to every online friend, including those not in the group, every thirty seconds, in exchange for a request that could no longer succeed. Both clients now skip it for private groups. Public groups, where this mechanism does work, are unchanged.

changes.title: Notification relay: an address header is checked to be an address
changes.description: The relay takes the caller's address from a header set by its front-end proxy, and used it both as the per-caller rate-limit key and in its own logs without checking it was an address at all. It is now parsed as one and ignored when it is not, so a value chosen by a caller cannot buy a separate rate-limit budget or place text of its choosing into the log an operator reads.

releases.title: Wake requests are now signed by the device that sends them
releases.summary: A short release with one change in it, and the change is that a mechanism which had been fully built finally started running. The signing was implemented on both apps and on the relay; what no shipped build carried was the key, so every release until this one went out with it switched off — and nothing said so.

changes.title: Notification wake requests carry a signature
changes.description: When your app asks the relay to wake somebody's device, that request is now signed. The signature covers the recipient, the sender and the time, so it cannot be replayed or reused for a different person, and the relay refuses a second use of the same one. Until this release the apps contained the code to do it and no key to do it with, which meant the check existed and never ran. The relay still accepts unsigned requests from older installations — refusing them today would silence notifications for everyone who has not updated — and will stop once enough of the installed base has moved over.

changes.title: The relay's own numbers are recorded with each release
changes.description: Deciding when it is safe to start refusing unsigned requests depends on knowing what share of real traffic is signed. That measurement is now captured from the running relay at the moment a release is cut and committed beside it, so the decision rests on a number taken at a known time rather than on a description written from memory. The threshold that has to be met is written down as figures, not as judgement.

releases.title: Who a message came from, and who may wake your phone
releases.summary: The largest security release so far, and most of it is about attribution: two places where the app showed a name it could not vouch for, and one where anyone holding your notification address could use it. Found by an outside review and a second, adversarial pass over the same code — every finding below had to survive somebody actively trying to disprove it.

changes.title: A relayed message can no longer carry an absent person's name
changes.description: When you join a group, other members send you the messages you missed. Each one names its author — and until now the app displayed that name on trust. If the author had been away long enough for the app to lose track of their signing key, whoever relayed the history could put their name on text they never wrote, and it appeared in the chat exactly as if they had. The rule is now the same for text and for files: if the relaying peer is not the author and the author's key cannot be checked, the message is kept but shown as relayed content of unknown authorship rather than as them. Nothing is silently dropped — losing real history is its own harm — but nothing borrows a name it has not earned.

changes.title: Your notification address no longer carries your token in the URL
changes.description: To be woken for a message while offline, your device gives each contact an address that the sender's app calls. That address used to carry your notification token as part of the web address itself, which meant it appeared in ordinary server logs. It now travels inside the request instead, where a web server does not write it down. Older installations still use the previous form and keep working; the retirement date for it is published in the project repository rather than decided quietly.

changes.title: Each contact gets its own key to wake you, and you can revoke one
changes.description: Knowing your notification address was previously enough to wake your device. Now each contact is given a separate per-contact credential, registered by your device after proving it holds the notification registration — a proof a contact cannot produce. Revoking one contact's credential stops that relationship and leaves every other one working. During the changeover the relay accepts both forms, so nobody's notifications break while the update spreads.

changes.title: iOS: per-contact credentials moved into the Keychain
changes.description: They were kept in the app's preferences file, which is included in an unencrypted device backup. They are now Keychain items marked as available only after the first unlock and only on this device, so they do not travel to a restored backup on different hardware. Existing installations move their stored values across once, on first launch after the update.

changes.title: Android: three permissions removed, two more bounded
changes.description: The app declared permission to draw over other apps, to dismiss the lock screen, and a vendor-specific thread-priority permission — and called none of them. A permission that grants nothing is still one an attacker inherits if the app is ever compromised, so they are gone. The two legacy storage permissions that remain are now limited to the Android versions that actually need them. Every permission the app requests is now listed in the repository with what asks for it, and the build fails if the two disagree.

changes.title: Android 8 is now the minimum
changes.description: The app declared support back to Android 5 while depending on platform behaviour that arrived in Android 8 — so on those versions parts of it never worked correctly, quietly. Google Play will no longer offer updates to devices below Android 8. Installed copies keep running; they simply stop receiving new versions.

changes.title: Desktop downloads are signed, and the page says how to check
changes.description: The Windows and macOS builds were unsigned, and the download page explained how to click past the operating system's warnings — which are the defence a substituted binary would have to get past. Each download now has a detached signature beside it, made with a key whose public half lives in the project's git repository rather than on the web server, so the file and the means of checking it travel by different routes. The verification command uses ssh-keygen, which is already present on macOS, Linux and Git for Windows.

changes.title: Website: stricter headers, and a check that they stay that way
changes.description: The site now sends a hash-based content policy, refuses to be framed, and declares a restrictive permissions policy. More usefully, an external check runs on a schedule and asserts all of it against the live site — the previous arrangement could only tell you what the configuration said, not what the server actually sent.

releases.title: Quieter, steadier background work
releases.summary: Three places threw an exception on every pass and caught it again — harmless in themselves, but they filled the log with stack traces and made real problems hard to see. Found by watching a phone's log for a minute rather than by reading code.

changes.title: Group maintenance no longer throws on every group
changes.description: The periodic check asked the database for a group's row and took the first result without checking there was one. For a group the network knows about but the database does not — which happens for a moment right after creating one — that threw, and the check runs for every group on every pass. It now asks for a single row and looks. If a group really has no database row, the log says so plainly instead of printing a stack trace: that state means the group cannot appear in the chat list, and it is worth seeing.

changes.title: No more exception on every screen resume
changes.description: Returning to the app hid a loading indicator that may not exist yet, throwing a null-pointer exception each time, and read the settings database before it was open — twice, once for the push token. All three are guarded now. The push token was already re-read later, so nothing was lost, but the app no longer starts by throwing three exceptions.

releases.title: Group chats get the same attachment folders as personal ones
releases.summary: The documents / audio / voice-notes split shipped for one-to-one chats earlier today now works in group chats too. Along the way the group chat stopped keeping three separate copies of the same database query — the reason a filter added in one place had no effect in the other two.

changes.title: Documents, audio and voice notes listed separately in a group
changes.description: The group chat's ⋮ menu now narrows the conversation to documents, to audio files, or to voice notes, and back to everything — the same four entries as a personal chat. Voice notes stay out of the audio list so the two are separate places to look. Verified on a phone: with a photo, a voice note and an mp3 in one group, each filter shows exactly its own kind.

changes.title: One query instead of three copies
changes.description: Opening a group, refreshing it and searching in it each ran their own copy of the same query. They now share one, so a change to what a group list shows cannot silently apply to one path and not the others.

releases.title: On smaller phones the keyboard covered the buttons — creating a group looked like it did nothing
releases.summary: A long-standing report finally reproduced: on a Samsung SM-A075F, creating a group did nothing at all — no error, no group. The cause was not group creation. On a 720x1600 screen the keyboard covers the bottom of the form, and the Cancel / Create buttons sat underneath it: you typed a name and there was simply nothing left to press. The same applied to creating a private group, joining a public group by id, and adding a contact. On taller phones the buttons stayed visible, which is why it never reproduced anywhere else.

changes.title: Create group, add contact and join group are usable on small screens again
changes.description: Since the app began targeting Android 15 the window is drawn edge to edge, and the old request to resize for the keyboard no longer has any effect — the layout keeps its full height and the on-screen keyboard is simply drawn over the bottom of it. The four form screens now lift their content by the height of the keyboard, so the buttons stay above it. Verified on the phone the report came from: both a public and a private group are created where nothing happened before.

releases.title: The emoji setting now survives closing the app
releases.summary: A follow-up to 0.2.34, found by restarting the app on a phone rather than trusting the code: the option that removes images of living beings from the emoji picker only took effect while the app stayed open. After a restart the full set came back, and the only way to get the filtered one again was to toggle the switch off and on.

changes.title: The emoji filter is applied at startup, not only when the switch is touched
changes.description: The emoji provider decides which categories exist at the moment it is installed, and the app installed it before reading the setting — so on every launch the unfiltered set was built, and the preference was read a fraction of a second too late. The setting is now read first, in both places the provider is installed, so a restart keeps what was chosen.

releases.title: The call screen belongs to you again, emoji can be kept free of living beings, and attachments split into files, audio and voice
releases.summary: A release driven almost entirely by what people reported. The video call screen was showing developer diagnostics to everyone — codec names, frame counters, an echo chip and two unlabelled sliders, one of which quietly set the volume of every later call; they are gone, and a tap on your own camera window now simply puts it away (a tap on the other person's video brings it back, a long press still enlarges it). At a user's request the emoji set can be kept free of images of living beings, with crosses, stars, zodiac signs, devils and LGBT symbols removed regardless of that setting, while the mosque, the Kaaba, the crescent and prayer beads stay. Attachments in a one-to-one chat can be listed as documents, audio or voice notes separately. And two things that made saving a photo pointless were fixed: the Save action no longer flashes and disappears, and a saved file really lands in Pictures / Movies / Download under a Khandaq folder, with the path shown, instead of a private directory no file manager opens.

changes.title: No more developer diagnostics on the call screen
changes.description: During a video call the screen carried a row of numbers meant for debugging — codec, resolution and frame counters, an echo-cancellation chip and two sliders with no labels. One of those sliders was a call volume that persisted into every later call, so a curious tap could leave someone permanently quiet. All of it is now confined to debug builds.

changes.title: Tapping your own camera window puts it away
changes.description: The little preview of your own camera used to react to a tap by growing, which read as "my camera now shows the other person" — the frame stayed on screen with the remote video showing through it. A tap now hides the preview and a tap on the other person's video brings it back at its normal size; a long press still enlarges it for anyone who used that.

changes.title: Emoji without images of living beings
changes.description: A setting in Settings removes faces, people and animals from the emoji picker. Independently of it — always — crosses, the Star of David, the six-pointed star, the menorah, yin-yang, om, the wheel of dharma, places of worship, all twelve zodiac signs, devils and demons, and pride and transgender flags including same-sex couples and families are gone from the set. The mosque, the Kaaba, the crescent with star, prayer beads and open hands remain.

changes.title: Attachments: documents, audio and voice notes separately
changes.description: The chat's ⋮ menu can now narrow a conversation down to documents, to audio files, or to voice notes, as well as back to everything. Voice notes are deliberately kept out of the audio list so the two are separate places to look rather than duplicates of each other.

changes.title: Saving a received file actually saves it
changes.description: Two defects met in the same place. The Save action appeared for a fraction of a second and vanished, and if you managed to hit it the message said the file had been saved to — with the path missing — while nothing had been written anywhere a file manager can reach. Files now go to Pictures, Movies or Download inside a Khandaq folder, the message names that folder, and a failure says so plainly instead of claiming success.

changes.title: Swipe between Chats, Groups and Favorites
changes.description: The three chat-list tabs can be moved between with a horizontal swipe on the list, instead of reaching up to the tabs themselves. The swipe respects right-to-left layout and stops at both ends rather than wrapping around.

changes.title: The in-app language reaches the whole interface
changes.description: Choosing a language in Settings changed the chat titles but left the bottom bar, the tab labels, the search field and the Edit button in the previous language, because those views had already been created by the time the language changed. The session is now rebuilt when the language changes, so everything follows it.

changes.title: Cancelling a selection no longer reloads every photo
changes.description: Leaving selection mode redrew the whole conversation, so every visible photo blanked and re-loaded from disk — a visible flicker on a screen full of images. Only the selection highlight is repainted now. Measured on a phone: 86% of the photo area changed before the fix, 0.3% after.

changes.title: Half-finished sign-up no longer closes the app
changes.description: If the app was relaunched while you were on the password step of creating an account, the screen came back but the name behind it did not, and continuing closed the app. It now returns you one screen back to retype the name.

changes.title: The active chat-list tab is announced to screen readers
changes.description: Which of Chats / Groups / Favorites is selected was conveyed by colour alone. The active tab is now marked as selected, so assistive technology says so.

releases.title: Relayed group history can no longer put words in someone else's mouth; four languages; a security audit closed out
releases.summary: A single entry covering everything between 0.2.12 and 0.2.31 — the site's changelog had fallen behind while releases kept going out through Google Play and TestFlight. The headline is authorship in groups: when a member's messages reach you second-hand, relayed by another member who was online at the time, the network can only vouch for whoever passed the message on — never for the person it names. Those messages now carry a signature from their real author, and anything relayed without one is marked in the chat as «sender not verified» instead of quietly looking the same as a message you received first-hand. Alongside that: the app is fully translated into English, Russian, Arabic (right-to-left) and Chinese with an in-app language picker, a second external security audit was worked through, and a long tail of group defects was fixed — a member who stayed invisible until you restarted the app, a group file that got stuck when sent while offline, and group video that never started.

changes.title: Group history now proves who wrote it
changes.description: Messages you were not online for arrive relayed by another member. Until now the app trusted the name that member attached to them — the encryption authenticates whoever relayed the message, never the author it claims. A member could therefore hand you a message that looks like it came from someone else in the group. Each author now signs their own messages with a signing key announced inside the group, receivers check that signature against the key they learned from that author directly, and the verdict is bound to the exact message — its author, its time and its text — so a genuine signature cannot be made to vouch for a different message.

changes.title: «Sender not verified» on relayed messages
changes.description: A group message that reached you second-hand and carries no valid signature is now marked as such in the chat, so an unproved claim about who wrote something no longer looks identical to a message you received directly from its author. The mark disappears on its own the moment a signature for that message arrives. Most messages are unmarked in practice: anything you receive while online comes straight from its author and is authenticated by the connection itself.

changes.title: Full localization: English, Russian, Arabic (RTL) and Chinese
changes.description: The apps are translated into four languages, with a language picker in Settings that no longer depends on the phone's system language. Arabic lays out right-to-left throughout, including chat headers, which previously clipped.

changes.title: Second external security audit worked through
changes.description: An independent review of the code produced ten findings; they were triaged one by one and fixed or closed with evidence. Among them: private one-to-one messages could be pulled into a group's history sync, an encrypted backup is now the default when you export a profile (and the export dialog no longer describes it inaccurately), history sync is bounded per group so a peer cannot make you spend the day fetching it, and every dependency pin in the release build is verified against upstream instead of being silently re-pinned by the build itself.

changes.title: Group defects: an invisible member, a stuck file, video that never started
changes.description: Three group problems that needed two devices to see at all. A member could stay invisible to you — with no way back short of restarting the app — after a one-way loss of visibility on the network. A file sent to a group while you were offline became a dead-end row: it could neither continue nor be cancelled. And group video could fail to start at all, silently. All three are fixed.

changes.title: Importing a profile brings the app back online by itself
changes.description: After importing a .tox profile the app used to sit unconnected until it was force-stopped, unless you pressed OK on the final dialog rather than leaving the screen. Worse, the imported profile was not being saved, so message edits, deletions and reactions quietly stopped arriving. The import now restarts the messaging engine on its own and the imported identity is stored properly. Note that only an unencrypted profile export can be imported — export from Settings rather than copying a file out of the app's storage.

changes.title: Long group messages keep their signature
changes.description: The signed copy of a very long group message was assembled slightly over the size limit the receiver enforces, so it was discarded on arrival without a word and the message stayed unverified for no visible reason. The limit is now derived from the packet size rather than set independently of it.

releases.title: Cross-platform video calls, Google Play release, iOS voice-note fix on older iPhones
releases.summary: The big one: 1:1 video calls now work end-to-end between Android and iOS. Both sides see each other's camera, the picture is upright and full-screen, and it keeps working after you switch apps and come back — previously the remote camera could show black, sideways, or freeze. Android is now published on the official Google Play Store (install and auto-update from there; the website links to Play instead of a sideload APK). On iOS, voice notes that silently failed to send on older iPhones (e.g. iPhone 11) now record and send reliably. The Android incoming-call screen was redesigned with the correct ringtone and accept-from-notification, right-to-left (Arabic) chat headers no longer clip, and both apps gained editing sent messages, reactions and delete-for-everyone across all message types, and swipe-to-reply.

changes.title: Cross-platform 1:1 video calls (Android ↔ iOS)
changes.description: Video calls between Android and iPhone now work in both directions. Each side sees the other's camera (the remote view was showing black before), the image is upright instead of sideways or upside-down, it fills the screen without letterbox bars, and the camera resumes correctly after you switch to another app and return. Under the hood the two platforms now negotiate the same video codec (VP8) and iOS renders incoming frames on a modern display layer.

changes.title: Android is now on Google Play
changes.description: Khandaq for Android is published on the official Google Play Store — install and get automatic updates from there. The website now links to the Play listing instead of hosting a sideload APK. If you are coming from an old sideloaded build, export your Tox profile first, then install from Play and import it (the app signing key is different).

changes.title: iOS — voice notes fixed on older iPhones
changes.description: On older iPhones (such as iPhone 11) a voice note would record while you held the mic but silently fail to send when you released. Recording now uses the correct audio session and the device's real sample rate, so voice notes capture and send reliably across all iPhone models.

changes.title: Android — redesigned call screen and ringtone
changes.description: The incoming-call screen was modernised: a proper ringtone that plays on the ringtone channel (instead of a mangled media sound), an Accept action directly from the call notification, a clean full-screen video layout, and the microphone/speaker routing is set up only once the call is accepted so early audio glitches are gone.

changes.title: Edit sent messages
changes.description: You can now edit a message you already sent — in 1:1 chats and groups. The recipient sees the updated text marked as edited. (Android already supported this; iOS now matches.)

changes.title: Reactions, delete-for-everyone and swipe-to-reply across all message types
changes.description: Emoji reactions and delete-for-everyone now work on photos, videos, voice messages and files — not just text — in both 1:1 chats and groups. Swipe a message to reply to it. Deleting for everyone reliably removes the message on the other person's device too.

changes.title: Android — right-to-left (Arabic) chat header no longer clips
changes.description: With an Arabic contact name the chat header and the 'online' status were being clipped or misaligned. The header now lays out correctly in right-to-left, in both 1:1 and group chats.

changes.title: Android — targets Android 16 and keeps your Tox ID across updates
changes.description: The app now targets Android 16 (API 36) for Google Play compliance, and updating the app no longer loses your Tox ID and contacts — the identity is recovered even if the encryption key drifted after a password change.

changes.title: Build, signing and website distribution hardening
changes.description: Following an external security review: the Android build can no longer be signed with a debug key by mistake, published checksums no longer leak build-machine paths, CI actions are pinned to exact versions, and the sideload APK was removed from the website and the release downloads in favour of Google Play.

releases.title: Android — design polish, Profile → Details, hold-to-record voice, friend-accept fix
releases.summary: More of the Android Figma pass plus a few fixes. The status bar now matches the toolbar (no more off-brand green), the bottom-nav icons are the new outlined set, photos and videos in chats are sized to hug the image instead of filling the row, and chats show the exact light/dark doodle wallpaper from the design. Profile gains a Details screen with an app lock (passcode + lock timeout), change password and delete profile. Voice messages switch to iOS-style hold-to-record — hold the mic to record, release to send, slide left to cancel — with a redesigned recording bar. The header theme toggle is gone (the Settings switch stays) and switching themes is now fast and smooth. Fixes a bug where messaging a contact who had just accepted your request was blocked with 'waiting for friend request'.

changes.title: Android — Profile → Details (app lock, change password, delete profile)
changes.description: A new Details screen under Profile: turn on an app lock that asks for your password when you reopen the app (with a lock-timeout option), change your password, or permanently delete the profile and all its data from the device.

changes.title: Android — messaging a freshly-accepted contact no longer blocked
changes.description: After you added someone and they accepted on their device, typing in the chat could still say 'Waiting for friend request to be accepted'. Messages now send and are delivered once the contact connects, instead of being blocked.

changes.title: Android — hold-to-record voice messages
changes.description: Voice messages now work like on iOS: press and hold the microphone to record, release to send, and slide left to cancel. The recording bar was restyled to match — timer, a blinking record dot and a large microphone button.

changes.title: Android — photos and videos sized to fit
changes.description: Media in chats no longer stretches across the whole row. Photos and videos now hug the image at a sensible size with rounded corners, keeping their aspect ratio, in both direct and group chats.

changes.title: Android — faster, smoother theme switching
changes.description: The sun/moon toggle was removed from the header (the dark-theme switch in Settings is enough), and switching between light and dark is now noticeably faster — it was rebuilding the screen twice.

changes.title: Android — design polish
changes.description: The system status bar now matches the toolbar instead of showing an off-brand green, the bottom navigation uses the new outlined icons, chats show the exact light/dark doodle wallpaper from the design, the profile MyID is shown as plain text, and the contact picker rows use clean letter avatars with an online/offline label.

changes.title: Android — cleaner media picker and import screen
changes.description: Picking a photo or video now opens the modern system photo picker (or a media-only picker on older devices) without the file-manager tabs, and the import-profile screen now describes the Android file-picker flow instead of the iOS one.

releases.title: Android — full Figma redesign: new headers, chat wallpaper, redesigned profile & settings, attachment-download control
releases.summary: The Android app gets the new Khandaq look across the board — onboarding, the chats list, conversations, contacts, settings and profile — with single-row chat headers, brand-teal accents, grouped setting cards and a proper light/dark theme. Conversations now show the Khandaq doodle wallpaper. Profile gains full-screen Name/Status editing and a MyID QR pop-up; Settings adds an Attachment download control (Never / Wi-Fi only / Always) and a dark-theme switch; Contacts gets an add button, a restyled add screen and a 'share your MyID' empty state; group chats get the same clean single-row header (avatar + member count + ⋮ menu). Also fixes the header theme toggle that flipped straight back to its previous mode.

changes.title: Android — full visual redesign to the new Khandaq look
changes.description: Onboarding, the chats list, conversations, contacts, settings and profile have been restyled to the new design: single-row chat headers, brand-teal accents, grouped cards and consistent light/dark theming. Secondary screens (group create/info, maintenance, share, about and more) now use the same clean light headers.

changes.title: Android — the header theme toggle now sticks
changes.description: Tapping the sun/moon icon in the header switched the theme but flipped straight back a moment later. The dark-mode switch's saved state was re-firing the toggle on screen recreation; it no longer does, so light/dark switching is reliable.

changes.title: Android — control how attachments download
changes.description: A new Settings → 'Attachment download' option lets you choose Never, Wi-Fi only or Always. It applies to both 1:1 and group chats, so incoming group files follow your choice instead of always downloading.

changes.title: Android — chat wallpaper
changes.description: Conversations (1:1, group and conference) now show the Khandaq doodle wallpaper behind messages, matching the design.

changes.title: Android — redesigned profile
changes.description: A card layout with avatar, full-screen Name and Status editing, a MyID card with copy-ID and a 'Show QR code' pop-up, the Tox capabilities row, and a Log out action.

changes.title: Android — redesigned settings
changes.description: Grouped cards with brand-teal switches (dark theme, notification preview, group system messages), profile export/import and the new attachment-download control.

changes.title: Android — redesigned contacts
changes.description: An add-contact button, a brand-aligned add-contact screen (with QR scan kept), and a 'you have no contacts yet' empty state that lets you copy your MyID or show your QR code so others can add you.

changes.title: Android — group chat single-row header
changes.description: Group chats now use the same clean one-row header as 1:1 chats: back, group avatar, name with member count, and a ⋮ menu holding search, members, add person and video.

releases.title: iOS polish — no more duplicate group messages, day separators, offline voice, delivery ticks & call fixes
releases.summary: A large iOS-focused round shipped to TestFlight (builds 142885–142899) from real-device QA. Headline fix: group messages no longer duplicate under different sender names. Chats gain Telegram-style day separators, inline photo/video previews with a play button, and sent/delivered ticks. Voice notes and files now queue while the recipient is offline and deliver once they reconnect (just like text). Names and nicknames stop resetting after a restart, video calls request camera access properly, the Licenses screen is readable in dark mode, and an empty-chat crash on the jump-to-latest button is fixed. Remote-camera display and call echo are still being worked on.

changes.title: iOS — group messages no longer duplicate
changes.description: The top reported pain: in groups a single message could appear many times under different sender names/roles. Tox relays carry the same message under a volatile peer id, so the de-duplication now keys on the stable message id + text on both the live and history-sync paths. Messages appear exactly once.

changes.title: iOS — voice notes & files deliver after the recipient comes back online
changes.description: Previously a voice message or photo sent while the other person was offline simply failed. Now it queues (like text) and is retried automatically every few seconds, so it arrives within moments of them reconnecting.

changes.title: iOS — names and nicknames stop resetting after a restart
changes.description: Custom nicknames and group member names persisted incorrectly and reverted on relaunch. They are now kept reliably across restarts (group peers are matched by their stable public key).

changes.title: iOS — files/audio received from Android now download
changes.description: Incoming audio and files from Android could fail with 'Download failed'. The file writer now ensures the destination exists, handles the placeholder cleanly and surfaces real errors, so transfers complete.

changes.title: iOS — crash fixed when tapping the jump-to-latest arrow in an empty chat
changes.description: In a chat with no messages the down-arrow button wrongly appeared and tapping it crashed the app. It is now hidden when there is nothing to scroll to, and the jump is guarded against an empty list.

changes.title: iOS — Telegram-style day separators in chats
changes.description: Messages are now grouped by day with a centered 'Today / Yesterday / date' chip above the first message of each day, in both 1:1 and group chats.

changes.title: iOS — photos and videos show inline previews
changes.description: Sent and received images and videos render as a proper thumbnail (with a play button for video) instead of a generic file row, matching the design and Android.

changes.title: iOS — delivery ticks for outgoing messages
changes.description: Outgoing messages now show a single tick when sent and a double tick once delivered.

changes.title: iOS — video call asks for camera access
changes.description: Starting or turning on video in a call now requests camera permission up front and shows a clear 'open Settings' prompt if denied, instead of a generic internal error. (Showing the other person's camera and removing call echo are still in progress.)

changes.title: iOS — Licenses screen readable in dark mode
changes.description: The acknowledgements/licenses text rendered as black-on-black in the dark theme; it now uses the theme text color and is readable.

changes.title: iOS — message captions shown even when the photo didn't load
changes.description: A caption attached to a photo is now shown as a normal message when the photo itself isn't displayed inline, so replies and text aren't lost behind a failed image.

changes.title: iOS — chat navigation and search polish
changes.description: Global search across all chats with tap-to-jump to a message, a jump-to-latest button, auto-scroll to the newest message after you send, a selected reply that survives leaving and re-entering a chat, and smoother day-chip scrolling.

changes.title: iOS — UI and theme fixes
changes.description: Filled the empty strip under the input bar, fixed the voice-recording bar overlap/background, kept the current tab when switching theme, restored chat-header avatars, tidied the navigation buttons, gave Saved Messages a bookmark icon, added a multi-line status field, and made MyID tap-to-copy.

releases.title: Stability, security & UX — crash fixes, accurate group counts, faster on old phones
releases.summary: Big round across all platforms: fixed a real-device iOS crash on group media, hardened security (Windows deps bumped past CVE-2023-5217, DB key never stored in plaintext, several pentest findings closed), made group member/online counts accurate and consistent across clients, auto-recovering and faster group/1:1 file transfers, full-length messages via chunking, Telegram-style single voice playback, camera-from-attach, and a performance pass that removes freezes on older Android phones. iOS via TestFlight (build 142852); Android and Desktop on the mirrors and GitHub.

changes.title: iOS — crash on sending/receiving group media fixed
changes.description: Sending a group photo or voice message, or retrying a photo, crashed on real devices (iPhone 16/17 Pro Max, iOS 26.6). Root cause: legacy group-file helpers queried the default (unencrypted) Realm, which became unmigratable after a schema bump and threw on every group file transfer. The default Realm config now self-heals. Confirmed fixed.

changes.title: Desktop (Windows) — bundled media/crypto libraries updated past known CVEs
changes.description: libvpx 1.11.0 → 1.14.0 (fixes CVE-2023-5217, a VP8 heap overflow), OpenSSL → 1.1.1w, FFmpeg → 4.4.5. The Windows cross-build was repaired end-to-end (libvpx mingw link, x264 build step, WinRT api-set false-positive) so these patched libraries actually ship.

changes.title: Security audit fixes (pentest findings closed)
changes.description: DB encryption key is no longer written to disk in plaintext — recovery uses a device-bound encrypted backup (NEW-3). Push-relay trusted-proxy handling so a client can't spoof its source IP (NEW-4). UnifiedPush URL validation tightened (NEW-1). Desktop image preview rejects decode-bombs and drops SVG (D-2). Filename/path-traversal hardening (D-3). NGC incoming-video bounds checks, ~30fps rate-limit and thread-safe peer map (D-4/5/6). Windows credential store NUL-terminates the user name (buffer over-read).

changes.title: Groups — messages, voice and files no longer show the wrong sender/name
changes.description: In NGC group chats a peer's voice/file/message could appear under another person's name (or your own), and 'X joined' notices showed wrong names — because the sender was resolved from a volatile peer id that NGC reuses when members leave and rejoin. The sender pubkey is now captured at the moment of receipt and all names resolve by stable pubkey, on both Android and iOS.

changes.title: iOS — sending video to a group fixed
changes.description: Videos picked for a group silently never sent: the file was copied on a background queue after the picker's temporary URL had already been deleted. The copy now happens synchronously while the URL is valid (photos were unaffected).

changes.title: Group member & online counts are now accurate and consistent
changes.description: Different clients showed different participant/online numbers for the same group. Both Android and iOS now read the counts straight from toxcore's NGC-synced group state (online peers incl. self + saved offline members), so clients converge on the same 'N members · M online'. The group-info screen and the in-group header also now agree.

changes.title: Group file transfers auto-recover (no more manual retry)
changes.description: A single dropped chunk left a group file stuck until the user tapped a retry circle. The receiver now re-requests missing chunks every few seconds (parity with iOS) instead of once per 30s, so transfers self-heal.

changes.title: Long messages send in full instead of being truncated
changes.description: Messages over ~1.3 KB were silently cut off. Long messages to an online friend are now split into chunks and reassembled on the other side; Saved Messages keep the full text. Pasting a very long message no longer freezes the input either.

changes.title: iOS — private (in-group direct) messages are surfaced
changes.description: A private message sent to you inside a group used to land silently with no alert. It now notifies like any message, titled '🔒 <sender> (private)', so you can tell it was addressed to you personally.

changes.title: Android — no more freezes on older phones
changes.description: Switching tabs/groups and opening busy chats could freeze the UI. Chat history now loads off the UI thread (1:1 and groups); per-row work in the chat/group lists (member counts, unread badges, icon drawables) is cached. Noticeably smoother on low-end devices.

changes.title: 1:1 files are accepted automatically
changes.description: Incoming files in a direct chat no longer show an accept/decline prompt — they download immediately, in both directions.

changes.title: Groups — photos and videos send and arrive reliably
changes.description: Group media could sit at 0% and end as 'Upload Failed', or (briefly) be blocked from sending. Sending now waits only for the group to be connected (the transfer broadcasts over the group mesh) and re-queues with auto-retry until the group is ready, instead of failing.

changes.title: Android — encrypted password-protected backup & restore
changes.description: New in Maintenance: create an encrypted .kbk backup of your whole profile (messages, media, contacts and identity) under a password (PBKDF2-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM), and restore it on a reinstall or a new device. The on-disk database/media stay encrypted; only the key and identity are wrapped under your password. Verified end-to-end on-device.

changes.title: Voice messages — only one plays at a time
changes.description: Starting a voice message now pauses whichever one was playing (Telegram-style), in both 1:1 and group chats.

changes.title: Message a group member privately
changes.description: Tapping a member opens their info with a clear 'Send private message' field and button (previously a hidden debug field that only sent on exit).

changes.title: Camera straight from the attach button
changes.description: The attach (paperclip) action now offers Camera (photo) / Record video / Gallery, so you can shoot and send media without leaving the chat.

changes.title: Send time shown for media in private/saved chats
changes.description: Voice messages, photos and videos in 1:1 and Saved Messages now show their send time, like text messages.

changes.title: Add-contact screen — Android-style on iOS, 'Paste ID' hint
changes.description: The iOS add-contact page now matches Android: 'Paste ID' field, 'Scan QR code' and a new 'Scan QR code from gallery' (decode a saved photo), plus a help line. Android ID hint renamed to 'Вставьте ID'.

changes.title: Connection-type diagnostic for group peers
changes.description: A peer's info now shows whether you reach them directly (UDP) or via a relay (TCP) — helpful for understanding transfer speed.

changes.title: Bootstrap from public Tox DHT nodes
changes.description: Both Android and iOS now bootstrap from the proven public Tox DHT (tox.abilinski.com, mf-net.eu, tox.initramfs.io, …) instead of self-hosted bootstrap nodes, so joining no longer depends on our own infra being reachable. The push.khandaq.org wake relay (FCM/APNs) is a separate role and is unchanged.

changes.title: Android — delivery status (checkmarks) on photos, videos, voice & files
changes.description: Outgoing media now shows the same status indicator as text: a clock while queued/awaiting the peer, a single check while transferring, and a double check once the recipient has pulled the whole file (real delivery for P2P transfers). Canceled transfers show no indicator.

changes.title: Android — faster group connect / reconnect
changes.description: Opening a group chat now forces an immediate reconnect of a stalled group instead of waiting out the back-off, and the automatic retry of a stuck announce starts at 6s instead of 15s. Rate-limited and connecting-safe, so it never interrupts an announce already in progress. Less time stuck on "Connecting…".

changes.title: Android — private (in-group direct) messages show as sent
changes.description: NGC private messages addressed to one group member used to sit on a clock forever (no delivery receipt exists for them). They now show as sent once delivered to the network.

changes.title: iOS — no more repeated 'joined the group' spam
changes.description: A peer reconnecting (or the app re-syncing the roster) no longer posts a fresh 'X joined the group' notice every time — only a genuine first join is announced.

changes.title: Android — profile import no longer freezes and fully replaces old data
changes.description: Importing a .tox profile used to block the UI thread while waiting for the network to stop (it felt frozen / "very slow") and, worse, only partly wiped the previous profile — old messages, files, transfers and relays were left behind and mixed into the imported account. Import now runs in the background behind a progress dialog and clears every table, so the imported profile comes in clean. Combined with the earlier fix, contacts keep their real names instead of becoming "friend #N".

releases.title: Android UX polish — chat media, favorites, profile tab
releases.summary: Android v0.2.7 (build 10299): Telegram-style media/file bubbles in groups, favorites tab fix, profile avatar on bottom nav, navigation and drawer cleanup. Desktop builds refreshed on mirrors. iOS unchanged — use TestFlight build 142825.

changes.title: Android — group media bubbles (Telegram-style)
